title: Returning to a photo shows the same editor preview as the first visit
highlight: Going back to a photo keeps the preview from the first visit.
notes: Decoded-cache entries outside the three most recently opened photos stay half-float. A return inside that window is the original full-precision buffer, so it costs no extra decode. A return outside it shows the expanded half-float preview immediately, then a cancellable background decode replaces it and bumps the preview-cache epoch so the final preview matches the first visit. Treating every half entry as a miss was rejected: warm editor decodes (bytes already in memory, cargo test profile, otherwise idle 8-core machine) took 353/433/338 ms on a 15MP ARW, 1280/1104/1070 ms on a 26MP RAF, and 787/901/816 ms on a 33MP ARW. Keeping only neighbours full was rejected because a later return would stay lossy.
